mainTopic: The נתינים, and when a סריס or איילונית is part of יבום and חליצה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the topic of the נתינים. רבי refused to permit them, because even if we give up our share in them, no one can give up the מזבח's share. רבי יוחנן holds the reverse. Then a new משנה begins: רבי יהושע heard two traditions, that a סריס does חליצה and that he does not. רבי עקיבא explains that a סריס אדם, who was once fertile, does חליצה, while a סריס חמה does not. רבי אליעזר says the opposite. The משנה adds that a סריס and an איילונית have no יבום or חליצה, and that relations with them count as בעילת זנות. The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא can allow a סריס אדם to do חליצה, since he treats a לאו like כרת. After the answers of רבי אמי and רבה are rejected, רב יוסף explains that for רבי עקיבא's school only לאוין of close relatives cancel a marriage. רבא then proves that fitness from an earlier time counts for ייבום, and the amud ends by beginning to define a סריס חמה.

steps.title: רבי refuses to permit the Gibeonites
steps.stepSummary: In רבי's time the חכמים wanted to permit the נתינים. רבי answered that even if we can give up our own share in them, nobody can give up the מזבח's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי, they wanted to permit the נתינים. רבי told them: We can give up our share, but who can give up the מזבח's share?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: the חכמים tried to permit the נתינים to marry Jews, and רבי stopped them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נתינים were given to serve both the community and the מזבח. רבי says the community could give up its own claim on them. But the מזבח's claim is not ours to cancel, so the נתינים stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The גבעונים, who were assigned as woodchoppers and water-drawers and are forbidden to marry into the community
To permit
Our share (the community's claim)
The altar's share

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ban on the נתינים is tied to their being assigned to two owners, the community and the מזבח.

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi
they sought to permit the Gibeonites.
Rabbi said to them:
Our share we can permit,
but the altar's share, who can permit?
phrases.notes: The 'shares' come from the פסוק that made them servants 'for the congregation and for the altar of ה'' (יהושע 9:27).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ban on the נתינים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נתינים cannot be permitted, because the מזבח's share in them cannot be released

steps.title: רבי יוחנן holds the reverse view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי argues with רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן says the community's share is forbidden forever, while the מזבח's share is permitted when there is no מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי חייא בר אבא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the community's share is always forbidden. The מזבח's share is forbidden while the מקדש stands, and permitted when it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רבי's view clashes with a teaching of רבי יוחנן and quotes that teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said 'our share' can be released, but the מזבח's share cannot, even though in his day there was no מקדש. רבי יוחנן says the opposite on both points. The community's share can never be released, and the מזבח's share falls away once the מקדש is destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: And this disagrees with
The congregation's share
Forever
The Temple is standing
Permitted (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the community's share can be released, but the מזבח's share cannot. רבי יוחנן: the community's share is forbidden forever, and the מזבח's share is permitted when there is no מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. They are exact opposites about which share is permanent.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba.
As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The congregation's share is forbidden forever;
the altar's share:
when the Temple is standing, it is forbidden;
when the Temple is not standing, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the story in step 1 conflicts with another opinion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The community's share is forbidden forever. The מזבח's share applies only while the מקדש stands.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's two conflicting traditions about a eunuch
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי יהושע heard one tradition that a סריס does חליצה and another that he does not, and he cannot explain the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I heard that a סריס does חליצה and his wife receives חליצה. I also heard that a סריס does not do חליצה and his wife does not receive חליצה. I can't explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. רבי יהושע presents two traditions that seem to contradict each other, which sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One tradition treats a סריס as part of the יבום system and the other leaves him out. רבי יהושע remembers both but not which case each one is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, the משנה
A man who cannot have children (eunuch)
Performs חליצה
I heard (a tradition from my teachers)
To explain

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yehoshua said: I heard
that a eunuch performs ḥalitza
and they perform ḥalitza with his wife,
phrases.notes: 'They' means his brothers, if he dies without children.

phrases.english: and that a eunuch does not perform ḥalitza
and they do not perform ḥalitza with his wife,
and I cannot explain it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions about a סריס and חליצה, and they seem to contradict each other

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: man-made eunuch versus eunuch from birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains the two traditions. A סריס אדם, who once was able to have children, does חליצה. A סריס חמה, who never was, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I will explain. A סריס made by man does חליצה, and his wife receives חליצה, because he once had a time of fitness. A סריס from birth does not do חליצה, and his wife does not receive חליצה, because he never had a time of fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא settles the contradiction by assigning each tradition to a different kind of סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is whether he ever had שעת הכושר, a time when he could have had children. Someone who once could have children belongs to the יבום system. Someone who never could is outside it from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A man made a eunuch by a person or an injury after birth
A man who has been a eunuch from birth
A time of fitness, when he could have had children
I will explain

steps.whatToRemember: סריס אדם once had שעת הכושר, so he does חליצה. סריס חמה never did, so he does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of שעת הכושר, a time when he was once fit, becomes the test for whether a man is part of יבום and חליצה at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: I will explain:
A eunuch caused by man
performs ḥalitza, and they perform ḥalitza with his wife,
because he had a time of fitness.
A eunuch by natural causes
phrases.notes: Literally 'a eunuch of the sun,' meaning he was already this way when he first saw the sun, at birth.

phrases.english: does not perform ḥalitza, and they do not perform ḥalitza with his wife,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: because he did not have a time of fitness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction רבי יהושע raised
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each tradition refers to a different kind of סריס
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two traditions seem to be talking about the same סריס and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: A סריס אדם does חליצה because he once had שעת הכושר. A סריס חמה does not, because he never had it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reverses רבי עקיבא's distinction
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the opposite of רבי עקיבא. A סריס חמה does חליצה because he can be cured, and a סריס אדם does not because he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Not so. A סריס חמה does חליצה, and his brothers do חליצה with his wife, because he has a cure. A סריס אדם does not do חליצה, and his brothers do not do חליצה with his wife, because he has no cure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי עקיבא and flips the two cases around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא looked at the past: was this man ever able to have children? רבי אליעזר looks at the future: can this man still be healed? A סריס חמה can be healed, so he counts like a regular brother. A סריס אדם cannot be healed, so he is left out of חליצה completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Not so; it is the other way around
A cure or healing
The brothers do חליצה with his widow

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use the same two cases, but they reach opposite results. For רבי עקיבא the סריס אדם does חליצה. For רבי אליעזר it is the סריס חמה who does.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Not so; rather:
A eunuch by nature performs ḥalitza
and they perform ḥalitza with his wife,
phrases.notes: "They" means his brothers. If he dies without children, they do חליצה with his widow.

phrases.english: because he can be cured.
A eunuch caused by man does not perform ḥalitza
and they do not perform ḥalitza with his wife,
because he cannot be cured.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to רבי עקיבא's distinction in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סריס חמה does חליצה because he can be cured. A סריס אדם does not, because he cannot be cured.

steps.title: Testimony about בן מגוסת supports רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן בתירא testified that בן מגוסת, a סריס אדם in ירושלים, had his wife taken in יבום. This supports רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן בתירא testified about בן מגוסת, who lived in ירושלים and was a סריס אדם. His brothers did יבום with his wife, which confirms the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A real case from ירושלים is brought to back up רבי עקיבא's view against רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said a סריס אדם is treated like a regular brother, so his widow falls to his brothers. בן מגוסת was a סריס אדם, and his widow actually received יבום. That fits רבי עקיבא and goes against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He testified
The name of a man in ירושלים who was a סריס אדם
To confirm or uphold the words of

steps.whyThisMatters: A testimony about something that actually happened is strong support. It shows how רבי עקיבא's view was followed in practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira testified
about ben Megusat, who was in Jerusalem,
a eunuch caused by man,
that they performed levirate marriage with his wife,
confirming the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי עקיבא (step 4) against רבי אליעזר (step 5)
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's view that the widow of a סריס אדם falls to his brothers
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case: the widow of בן מגוסת, a סריס אדם, received יבום

steps.title: A סריס and an איילונית do neither חליצה nor יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סריס does not do חליצה or יבום. Likewise, an איילונית does not receive חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סריס does not do חליצה and does not do יבום. Likewise, an איילונית does not receive חליצה and does not receive יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new general rule that leaves the סריס and the איילונית out of the whole system of יבום and חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This סריס is the kind who never had שעת הכושר (a סריס חמה, as in רבי עקיבא's view), and the איילונית also never could have children. So the system does not apply to them at all. The man cannot do יבום or חליצה, and the woman cannot receive either one.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is physically unable to have children
Does יבום (marries his dead brother's widow)
Receives יבום

phrases.english: A eunuch neither performs ḥalitza nor levirate marriage,
and likewise an aylonit
neither receives ḥalitza nor levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling in the משנה about the סריס and the איילונית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סריס and an איילונית have no חליצה and no יבום.

steps.title: Their חליצה does not disqualify her, but their relations do
steps.stepSummary: If a סריס does חליצה, it does not disqualify the woman. If he has relations with her, she is disqualified, because it counts as בעילת זנות. The same holds for an איילונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a סריס did חליצה with his יבמה, he did not disqualify her. If he had relations with her, he did disqualify her, because it is בעילת זנות. Likewise, if the brothers did חליצה with an איילונית, they did not disqualify her. If they had relations with her, they disqualified her, because those relations are בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens if they went ahead and did חליצה or יבום anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their חליצה does not count at all, so the woman does not get the status of a חלוצה. Relations are different. Since there is no real מצוה of יבום here, the relations are forbidden relations, called בעילת זנות, and that disqualifies her.

keyTerms.meaning: He disqualified her (from marrying a כהן)
Forbidden relations that are not a מצוה
His dead brother's widow

steps.whatToRemember: An empty חליצה does nothing. Relations without a real מצוה of יבום count as בעילת זנות and do disqualify the woman.

phrases.english: A eunuch who performed ḥalitza with his yevama
has not disqualified her.
phrases.notes: He means she is not made unfit to marry a כהן.

phrases.english: If he had intercourse with her, he disqualified her,
because it is licentious intercourse.
And likewise an aylonit with whom the brothers performed ḥalitza
they have not disqualified her.
If they had intercourse with her, they disqualified her,
because her intercourse is licentious intercourse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7 by explaining the result if they did חליצה or יבום anyway
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their חליצה does not disqualify the woman. Their relations do disqualify her, because they are בעילת זנות.

steps.title: How can a סריס אדם do חליצה if רבי עקיבא treats a לאו like כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא using his own known rule. A סריס אדם is forbidden by a לאו, and רבי עקיבא treats that like כרת, which rules out חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know that רבי עקיבא holds that people forbidden by a לאו are like people forbidden by כרת. People forbidden by כרת cannot do חליצה or ייבום. So how can a סריס אדם do חליצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a question on רבי עקיבא's ruling that a סריס אדם does חליצה. His own rule elsewhere seems to say he should not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סריס אדם is forbidden by a לאו from marrying a Jewish woman. רבי עקיבא holds that a לאו works just like כרת, so the marriage does not take effect. Since people forbidden by כרת are not part of חליצה and ייבום, a סריס אדם should not be either.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Now, since; opens a question built on something we already know
People forbidden to each other by a regular negative command
People forbidden to each other with the punishment of כרת

phrases.english: Gemara: Now, we have heard that Rabbi Akiva
said: those who are liable for a prohibition
phrases.notes: A סריס אדם falls into this group. He is forbidden by a לאו from marrying into the קהל (דברים 23:2).

phrases.english: are like those liable for karet,
and those liable for karet
are not subject to halitza and yibum!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by questioning רבי עקיבא's ruling from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that a סריס אדם does חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's own rule makes a לאו equal to כרת, and כרת cases have no חליצה. So a סריס אדם, who is forbidden by a לאו, should have no חליצה.

steps.title: The case is where the brother married a convert
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that the brother's wife was a convert. רבי עקיבא follows רבי יוסי, who says converts are not called the 'קהל', so a סריס may marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: The case is where the brother married a convert. רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי יוסי, who said that a group of converts is not called the 'קהל'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question by narrowing the case to a widow who is a convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו only forbids a סריס from marrying into the 'קהל'. If converts are not counted as the 'קהל', there is no לאו at all with a convert. Without a לאו, the question from the rule 'a לאו is like כרת' disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a ruling to a specific case
A woman who converted
The community of converts
The 'congregation' that a סריס may not marry into

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where his brother married a convert,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: the congregation of converts
is not called a 'congregation.'
phrases.notes: So the לאו that keeps a סריס from 'the קהל' does not cover a convert. He is allowed to marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the widow was a regular Jewish woman, forbidden to the סריס by a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The widow is a convert. Following רבי יוסי, she is not part of the 'קהל', so there is no לאו.

steps.title: Then he should be able to do full ייבום too
steps.stepSummary: If there is no prohibition at all, the סריס should be allowed to do ייבום, not just חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also be able to do ייבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אמי's answer. If the convert is fully permitted, why did רבי עקיבא only mention חליצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no לאו, nothing stops the סריס from marrying her. Yet the משנה quotes רבי עקיבא as saying only 'חולץ'. That suggests ייבום is not allowed, which seems to clash with רבי אמי's case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a problem that comes from the last answer
He could actually do ייבום

phrases.english: If so,
he should also be able to perform yibum!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's explanation that the widow was a convert
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no prohibition applies, full ייבום should be allowed. So why did רבי עקיבא say only חליצה?

steps.title: Yes, he can do ייבום. רבי עקיבא just matched רבי יהושע's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that ייבום is allowed. רבי עקיבא said 'חולץ' only because he was replying in the language רבי יהושע had used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But since רבי יהושע said 'he does חליצה', רבי עקיבא also said 'he does חליצה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and explains why רבי עקיבא's wording only mentioned חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legally, the סריס אדם may do either ייבום or חליצה with the convert. The word 'חולץ' is not a limit on the law. It is just a borrowed phrase from רבי יהושע's statement, which רבי עקיבא was explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, it is indeed so; agreeing with the challenge
Since; because of the other wording

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'חולץ' here as 'only חליצה, no ייבום.' The גמרא is saying ייבום is allowed too. The word חליצה was just copied from רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
but since Rabbi Yehoshua said 'he performs halitza,'
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה, where רבי יהושע said he had heard that a סריס does חליצה.

phrases.english: he also said 'he performs halitza.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing with the point and explaining the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's word 'חולץ' implies ייבום is not allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: ייבום is allowed. 'חולץ' only echoes רבי יהושע's language.

steps.title: The משנה's wording proves ייבום was allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer from the testimony about בן מגוסת. It mentions actual ייבום as following רבי עקיבא's view, so it concludes this reading is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too. The משנה teaches that רבי יהושע בן בתירא testified about בן מגוסת in ירושלים, a סריס אדם, and that they did ייבום with his wife, to support רבי עקיבא. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the משנה itself and then concludes 'שמע מינה,' meaning this explanation is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony was given to support רבי עקיבא, and it uses the word ייבום, not just חליצה. That shows רבי עקיבא allows full ייבום in a case like this, just as step 12 said. The 'שמע מינה' closes the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also exact; the wording itself supports what we said
Testified
To support and uphold the words of
Learn from this; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's answer: רבי עקיבא's case is a widow who is a convert, who is not part of the 'קהל' (following רבי יוסי), so the סריס אדם may even do full ייבום. Step 14 attacks this answer, and the גמרא later replaces it.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira testified
about ben Megusat, who was in Jerusalem,
a eunuch caused by man, and they performed yibum with his wife
to uphold the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for the answer in step 12, then concludes.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא allows full ייבום for a סריס אדם in the case of a convert
steps.raayaSupportSource: The testimony of רבי יהושע בן בתירא about בן מגוסת in the משנה, which says 'ויבמו' to support רבי עקיבא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Within רבי אמי's approach, רבי עקיבא allows ייבום, and 'חולץ' was only borrowed wording. רבה challenges the whole approach in the next step.

steps.title: רבה's objection from a teaching about injured men
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a ברייתא in which a פצוע דכא, כרות שפכה, סריס אדם and an old man do חליצה or ייבום with their brothers' wives. The ברייתא supports the rule with the פסוק about not entering the קהל, so these women are full members of the קהל, not converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: a ברייתא teaches that a man with crushed testicles, a man whose organ is cut off, a man-made סריס, and an old man can do חליצה or ייבום. How so? If these men died leaving wives and brothers, and the brothers did מאמר, gave a גט, or did חליצה, what they did counts, and if they had relations they acquired the women. If the brothers died and these injured men did מאמר, gave a גט, or did חליצה with the brothers' wives, what they did counts. If they had relations they acquired them, but they may not stay married to them, because the פסוק says an injured man may not enter the קהל of ה׳. So we must be dealing with a woman who is in the קהל!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רבי אמי's answer that the woman in רבי עקיבא's case was a convert. He brings a ברייתא where injured men do חליצה even with women who are part of the קהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the injured man's ייבום works but he may not keep her, and it quotes the פסוק of 'בקהל ה׳'. That only makes sense if the woman is a born Jew who is part of the קהל. Even so, the ברייתא allows חליצה, so the convert explanation cannot be the reason a סריס does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: a man whose testicles are crushed
a man whose organ has been cut off
a rabbinic betrothal done by the יבם before ייבום
forbidden to keep them as wives
so clearly / this shows that

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא has two halves. In the first half the injured men are the ones who died, so their healthy brothers do the ייבום. In the second half the injured men are the living brothers, and that is the half רבה's objection is built on.

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
A man with crushed testicles and a man whose organ is cut off,
a eunuch made by man, and an old man —
either do חליצה or do ייבום.
How so? If they died and they had wives,
and they had brothers,
and the brothers went and did מאמר with their wives,
and gave a גט, or did חליצה —
what they did is done,
and if they had relations, they acquired them.
If the brothers died,
phrases.notes: Now it flips: the healthy brothers died, and the injured men are the ones left alive.

phrases.english: and they went and did מאמר with their wives,
and gave a גט or did חליצה —
what they did is done.
And if they had relations, they acquired them,
but it is forbidden to keep them,
because it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יָבֹא פְצוּעַ דַּכָּא וּכְרוּת שׇׁפְכָה בִּקְהַל ה׳״,
phrases.english: "A man with crushed testicles or a cut-off organ shall not enter the congregation of ה׳",
So clearly we are dealing with a woman in the congregation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the convert explanation that steps 10-13 built up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's explanation that רבי עקיבא's סריס case involves a convert woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets injured men do חליצה even with women who are in the קהל, as its proof-פסוק shows. So the reason a סריס does חליצה cannot be that the woman is a convert.

steps.title: The man was injured only after the יבמה fell to him
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the case is one where the brother died while the man was still healthy, so the יבמה fell to him. He was injured only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: the case is where she fell to him for ייבום, and only afterward was he injured.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה drops the convert explanation and gives a new case. At the moment the brother died, the living brother was healthy, and he became injured only later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the יבמה fell to him while he was still fit, the ייבום connection started out properly. That is why חליצה (and ייבום) can still work even after he became injured.

keyTerms.meaning: she fell to him, meaning she became bound to him for ייבום
and afterward he was injured

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question for what follows: does a prohibition that arrives after the יבמה has already fallen push away the ייבום?

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
for example, where she fell to him,
phrases.notes: His brother died while he was still healthy, so the widow became bound to him for ייבום.

phrases.english: and in the end he was injured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's own objection with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (the timing of the injury).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי עקיבא's case only works if the woman is a convert.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where the injury happened after the יבמה had already fallen to him.

steps.title: אביי: the later prohibition should push away the ייבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: once the man is injured, the prohibition of פצוע דכא should come and push aside the מצוה of ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let the prohibition of an injured man come and push aside the positive מצוה of ייבום!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's new case. He says that even if the injury came later, the prohibition should still cancel the ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer depends on the ייבום connection starting before the injury. אביי argues that a prohibition that arrives later can still push the מצוה of ייבום away, so רבה's timing should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: let it come
and push aside
the positive מצוה of ייבום

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
Let the prohibition of an injured man come
and push aside the positive mitzvah of ייבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְלַיְתֵי אִיסּוּר פָּצוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's case where the injury came after the יבמה fell to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition that arrives later should still push away the מצוה of ייבום, so the timing should not save the case.

steps.title: אביי begins a proof from רבן גמליאל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts quoting a משנה in which רבן גמליאל rules that if a young girl refuses her marriage (מיאון), her refusal works. The quote continues in step 18.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn in a משנה: רבן גמליאל says, if she refused, she has refused,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: אביי begins quoting a משנה to back up his challenge. The rest of the quote and the point he draws from it come in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מי לא תנן' tells us a known משנה is being brought as support. So far we have only the start of רבן גמליאל's ruling about מיאון. How it shows that a later prohibition pushes away ייבום will become clear once the quote is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: didn't we learn in a משנה?
she refused, meaning a young girl married by rabbinic law cancels the marriage

phrases.english: Didn't we learn in a משנה,
רבן גמליאל says:
if she refused, she has refused,
phrases.notes: This is a young girl married off by her family under rabbinic law. She can cancel the marriage just by refusing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא תְּנַן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support אביי's challenge in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that a later prohibition can push away the מצוה of ייבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבן גמליאל's ruling about מיאון (quote continues in step 18).

steps.title: End of the משנה: a wife's sister pushes aside ייבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes quoting רבן גמליאל's ruling. If the minor does not refuse, she waits until she is an adult, and then her older sister goes free as a wife's sister. אביי infers that the prohibition of אחות אשה pushes aside the מצוה of ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she does not refuse, she must wait until she grows up, and then the other sister goes free because she is his wife's sister. So we see that the prohibition of a wife's sister comes and pushes aside ייבום.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes the משנה he began quoting and draws a lesson from it. He sets up the proof that a prohibition which shows up later can push aside ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the older sister was waiting for ייבום. Once the minor becomes an adult, her marriage is fully valid, and the older sister becomes 'his wife's sister.' That later prohibition cancels the ייבום that was in place before.

keyTerms.meaning: She must wait until she becomes an adult
A wife's sister, a forbidden relative (an ערוה)
So we see / apparently, used to draw a conclusion
Pushes aside / overrides

phrases.english: And if not,
she must wait until she grows up,
and this one goes out free,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the older sister who was waiting for ייבום.

phrases.english: because she is his wife's sister.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא: אָתֵי אִיסּוּר אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה וְדָחֵי.
phrases.english: So we see: the prohibition of a wife's sister comes and pushes aside the ייבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא: אָתֵי אִיסּוּר אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה וְדָחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quote begun in Step 17 and draws the inference from it.
steps.raayaObject: A prohibition that starts after the יבמה has already fallen to the brother can still push aside ייבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבן גמליאל about the minor sister who does not refuse.

steps.title: So the injury prohibition should also push aside ייבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי applies the lesson: just as the wife's sister prohibition pushes aside ייבום, the prohibition of פצוע דכא should push it aside too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let the prohibition of an injured man come and push aside ייבום!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses the proof to knock down רבה's answer from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the man was healthy when his brother died and was only injured later. אביי replies that a prohibition arising later can still override ייבום, as the משנה shows. So the timing does not save רבה's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, applying the same logic to our case
A man injured in his reproductive organs (פצוע דכא)

phrases.english: Here too,
let the prohibition of an injured man come and push it aside!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי: נֵיתֵי אִיסּוּר פָּצוּעַ וְנִידְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the proof from Step 18 to the case of פצוע דכא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's answer in Step 15 that the man was healthy when the יבמה fell to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition that comes later still overrides ייבום, so a later injury should override it too.

steps.title: רב יוסף: This תנא follows the school of רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new answer. The ברייתא follows the school of רבי עקיבא, which holds that only incest prohibitions (שאר) produce a ממזר. Plain prohibitions like פצוע דכא are weaker and do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: This תנא is the תנא of the school of רבי עקיבא, who said that from people liable for incest prohibitions a ממזר is born, but from people liable for ordinary prohibitions no ממזר is born.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף drops רבה's answer and explains the ברייתא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף goes back to the original question in step 9. That question assumed רבי עקיבא treats every לאו like כרת, so the marriage of a סריס אדם would not take effect. This תנא of רבי עקיבא's school treats only לאוין of close relatives (שאר) that way. A plain לאו, like the ban on a פצוע דכא, does not cancel the marriage, so his wife is a real wife and he is part of חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, signals dropping the earlier answer
The teacher of the school of רבי עקיבא
Those who break negative commandments involving close relatives
Plain, ordinary negative commandments
A child born from a forbidden union

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a פצוע דכא is allowed to marry a Jewish woman. He is still forbidden. The point is only that his prohibition is a plain לאו, too weak to push aside ייבום.

phrases.english: Rather, רב יוסף said:
This תנא

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: is that תנא of the school of רבי עקיבא,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מֵחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין דִּשְׁאֵר הָוֵי מַמְזֵר,
phrases.english: who said: from those liable for prohibitions of close relatives, a ממזר is born,

phrases.aramaic: מֵחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין גְּרִידִי לָא הָוֵי מַמְזֵר.
phrases.english: from those liable for ordinary prohibitions, no ממזר is born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by giving up רבה's approach and explaining the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא (רבי עקיבא's school) who ranks prohibitions differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא treats every לאו like כרת, so the marriage of a סריס אדם (forbidden by a לאו) would not take effect, and he would have no חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For this תנא of רבי עקיבא's school, only לאוין of close relatives (שאר) make the marriage fail. The plain לאו of פצוע דכא does not, so his marriage holds and he does חליצה.

steps.title: He can't 'establish a name for his brother'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ייבום can apply to a man who can no longer have children. The פסוק says ייבום is 'to establish a name for his brother,' and he is unable to do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read here: 'to establish a name for his brother.' And this man is not capable of that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge from the פסוק itself against letting a סריס or injured man do ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose of ייבום is to have a child in the dead brother's name. A man who cannot father children now cannot fulfill that purpose. Being fertile at some earlier time should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Read here, apply this פסוק to our case
To establish a name for his brother, the purpose of ייבום
Capable of this

phrases.english: Read here
"to establish a name for his brother,"
and this one is not capable of that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the ברייתא's ruling, based on the purpose stated in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling in the משנה that a סריס אדם does חליצה because he once had שעת הכושר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ייבום exists to produce a child for the dead brother. A man who can no longer father children cannot do that.

steps.title: רבא: Then no woman could ever have ייבום
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the challenge. If only the very last moment counted, no woman would be fit for ייבום, because every husband becomes sterile like a סריס חמה a little before he dies. So earlier fitness must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If so, there is no woman fit for ייבום, since her husband surely became a natural סריס one hour before his death!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the challenge from Step 21 by showing it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being fertile earlier did not count, then even the dead husband, who surely lost his fertility right before death, would be treated as a סריס. His wife could never have ייבום. Since ייבום clearly exists, earlier fitness must be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, introduces an argument that leads to an impossible result
A man who is sterile by nature, not because of an injury
One hour before his death

steps.whatToRemember: Per רב יוסף, the תנא of רבי עקיבא's school holds that the plain לאו of פצוע דכא does not cancel a marriage, so a סריס אדם is part of חליצה. Fitness from an earlier time counts for ייבום, or else no woman could ever have ייבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the principle that fitness for ייבום is judged by an earlier time, not by the last moment.

phrases.english: רבא said: If so,
you have no woman who is fit for ייבום,
since her husband surely became a natural סריס
one hour before his death!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, אֵין לְךָ אִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּשֵׁרָה לְיַבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 21 by showing its logic leads to an impossible result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that only present ability to have children counts for ייבום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Every husband loses his fertility shortly before death, so that rule would wipe out ייבום entirely.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reductio: the challenge's logic would wipe out ייבום entirely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only present ability to have children counts, so a man who was once fertile but no longer is cannot do ייבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Earlier fitness counts, since every husband loses his fertility shortly before death and ייבום still applies.

steps.title: רבא's argument seems to refute רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's proof, that earlier fitness counts, contradicts רבי אליעזר. He rules that a סריס אדם does not do חליצה, even though he was once able to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, רבא's answer is actually a refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבא's argument from Step 22 against רבי אליעזר in the משנה. If earlier fitness counts, רבי אליעזר's ruling seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says a man who was made a סריס by a person does not do חליצה, even though he was once fertile. רבא argued that a dying husband is also unable to have children at the end, yet ייבום still applies, so earlier fitness must count. By that same logic, the סריס אדם's earlier fitness should count too, which goes against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: An answer or resolution to a problem
A refutation, something that knocks down a position
A man made unable to have children by an injury or act of a person
A time when he was fit, here meaning able to have children

phrases.english: According to רבי אליעזר,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר in our משנה, who says a סריס אדם does not do חליצה.

phrases.english: Rava's answer is a refutation!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, פֵּירוּקָא דְרָבָא פִּירְכָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבא's rejection in Step 22 and shows it clashes with רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a סריס אדם does not do חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If earlier fitness counts for a dying husband (רבא), it should also count for a סריס אדם who was once fertile. Yet רבי אליעזר excludes him.

steps.title: A dying man only has weakness that has set in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבי אליעזר. A dying man is different, because he only has a general weakness that has begun in his body. A סריס אדם has actual damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a weakness that has begun in him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר. It shows that the dying husband's case and the סריס אדם's case are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dying man cannot have children only because the weakness of approaching death has taken hold of him. His body itself is not damaged. The סריס אדם has real damage to his body. So רבא's proof about dying men says nothing about a סריס אדם, and רבי אליעזר's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other case (the dying man)
Weakness, physical frailty

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying a dying man is fine for ייבום while a סריס is not because of timing. The difference is the kind of problem: general weakness versus real bodily damage.

phrases.english: There, it is a weakness that has begun in him.
phrases.notes: "There" means the dying husband from רבא's argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): general weakness versus bodily damage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dying man and a סריס אדם are alike, since both were once fertile and later were not.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dying man only has the weakness of approaching death, while a סריס אדם is damaged. So רבא's proof does not refute רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It lets רבא's principle and רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה both stand side by side.

steps.title: What counts as a natural-born eunuch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical definition of a סריס חמה. רב יצחק בר יוסף begins to answer in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a סריס חמה? רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, practical question: how do we recognize a סריס חמה? The answer starts here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the rules for different kinds of סריס. Now the גמרא wants signs that identify a man born unable to have children. This matters because the משנה treats a סריס חמה differently from a סריס אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look in practice?
A man born unable to have children (literally, a סריס from the sun, meaning from birth)

phrases.english: What is the case of a natural-born eunuch?
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said: Anyone
